Delta Air Lines waited seven years to bring back nonstop flights between New York JFK and Orange County. Now, just six months after their return, the airline is preparing to suspend them again.

Delta relaunched the route in May 2026, offering daily flights aboard Boeing 757-200s equipped with 16 lie-flat Delta One seats. The service gave passengers another premium option between New York and Southern California without having to travel through Los Angeles International Airport.

But according to Cirium schedule data cited by Simple Flying, Delta’s final flights are scheduled for November 29, with service expected to resume on May 6, 2027.

That leaves American Airlines as the only carrier operating nonstop between JFK and Orange County during Delta’s absence.

American has served the route since July 2021 and plans to continue flying daily. Its premium Airbus A321T aircraft offer 30 lie-flat seats, although the airline is gradually replacing that configuration as its new A321XLRs enter service.

United also connects Orange County with the New York area, but flies to Newark rather than JFK.

Delta hasn’t publicly explained the upcoming pause, so there’s no confirmed reason to suggest the route has underperformed.

Still, it’s an interesting reversal for a service that only returned in May. American spent years flying the route without Delta, briefly gained a competitor, and is now set to have JFK–Orange County to itself again until next spring.

text:
Paper: Same Inducement, Different Packaging — Cigarette Trades and Free-Food Ballot Events in California

Both the Skid Row cigarette-for-signature schemes and the Republican free-food ballot events rely on the same basic mechanism: a tangible benefit is used to move election documents. The difference is packaging. One version is a direct exchange that violates existing law and has been filmed and prosecuted. The other embeds the benefit inside a social event so that it remains legal under California’s current rules. Republicans running the food events are not inventing a new practice; they are adapting an existing incentive structure to the legal environment Democrats created and expanded.

 The Direct Version
On Skid Row, circulators offered cigarettes or a few dollars specifically in return for a signature on an initiative petition, and sometimes on a voter registration form. California Elections Code § 18603 makes it a misdemeanor to offer or give money or other valuable consideration in exchange for a petition signature. Undercover videos repeatedly captured these trades. Prosecutors treated the cigarettes as valuable consideration. The result was state charges in the 2016–2018 cycles with multiple guilty pleas, followed by later federal cases that involved the use of stolen voter identities. The transaction was simple and open: the item was conditioned on the signature. That is why enforcement followed.

 The Packaged Version
Republican groups, most visibly Carl DeMaio’s Reform California, host free food and drink events while people complete ballots, receive voter guides, and optionally leave their completed ballots for collection and delivery. Third-party ballot return is legal in California. The food is presented as hospitality at a political gathering rather than as payment for a signature or a vote. Under the 2025 statute (§ 18107.5), an offense requires either intent to induce voting or registration or a benefit that is contingent on the person actually voting or registering. Open free food without an explicit contingency has not produced the same enforcement. Earlier case law involving free tacos available to anyone, without conditioning them on voting, was not treated as illegal vote-buying. Organizers can therefore describe the events as ordinary turnout encouragement while still collecting ballots.

 Why the Packaging Works
DeMaio and similar Republicans state the strategy openly. Democrats legalized and used aggressive ballot collection after 2016–2018, and it contributed to Republican losses. Opposing the practice while refusing to use it is, in their view, self-defeating, so they match it under the existing rules and call their version “ballot harvesting done right.” The free food gets people to attend, stay, and hand over ballots without creating a recorded “pay for signature” exchange. Other California Republicans have promoted comparable “bring your own ballot” parties with food. From the perspective that treats both practices as the same underlying inducement, the cleverness consists of converting an activity that has been prosecuted when done directly into one that has not been prosecuted when staged as an event.

 Substance Versus Form
The practical effect in both settings is that more election paperwork moves because something of value was provided. In one case the benefit is small, immediate, and conditioned on the act, which violates § 18603. In the other the benefit is larger, social, and not formally conditioned, which has so far avoided liability under § 18107.5. The distinction is real under the statutes as written and enforced; whether it is meaningful depends on whether one focuses on the letter of the law or on the shared incentive structure. To date, the cigarette-for-signature exchanges have produced prosecutions. The free-food ballot events have not. That gap is the product of how the offer is structured, not the absence of an inducement.

A POWERFUL ARTICLE BY SUSAN B. GLASSER IN THE NEW YORKER: IS TRUMP HELPING PUTIN WIN?

Trump’s Republican Party is barely holding on to both chambers of Congress, while his approval ratings are sinking to historic lows. Yet at this critical moment, the president has spent an entire week attacking Volodymyr Zelensky and openly helping Vladimir Putin in his war of aggression against Ukraine.

Zelensky is now publicly describing his conflict with Trump as an almost irreversible rupture. Ukraine is “losing a strong partner,” he told Piers Morgan. “It hurts when Trump chooses a side, and it isn't ours.” In an interview with the Financial Times, Zelensky also announced that Ukraine had observed Trump’s proposed energy ceasefire for three days but would no longer comply, despite American threats to suspend intelligence sharing. “That’s over,” he declared.

Timing is everything, both in war and in midterm elections. And this particular moment is extraordinarily dangerous. Trump’s special envoys are once again pressuring Kyiv to accept an agreement that looks far more like surrender than compromise.

“The moment of greatest danger is now,” warned Daniel Fried, a former senior American diplomat. Returning from meetings with security officials in Poland and Romania, Fried expressed deep concern not only about Ukraine’s position but also about Russia’s escalating attacks designed to test NATO allies. His greatest fear is that Putin recognizes this vulnerability and intends to exploit it immediately.

The question is whether anyone in Washington can—or even wants to—stop him, given Trump’s expansive interpretation of presidential authority and his apparent indifference to Congress.

Senator Chris Coons of Delaware offered an equally disturbing assessment. Trump’s worst instincts, he argued, continue to prevail: trusting Putin and treating the Russian dictator’s words as more important than the warnings of America’s allies.

Coons recalled the enormous effort required to persuade Trump to sign the Graham sanctions legislation against Russia. Now Trump has undermined his own Ukraine strategy, repeating a pattern that has become painfully familiar over the past decade. He takes a hesitant step toward helping Kyiv, speaks with Putin, and promptly returns to his instinctive preference for Moscow.

Can America repair its damaged relationship with European allies? Coons answered his own question: “Not while Trump is president.” He also warned that the damage Trump could inflict over the next two years is being seriously underestimated.

Even Republicans are increasingly alarmed. Six Republican senators recently condemned Trump’s Russian diesel agreement as a gift to an adversary and a betrayal of allies. The Wall Street Journal’s editorial board called it a moral and strategic mistake, an assessment quickly amplified by Trump’s former vice president, Mike Pence.

Meanwhile, a new Fox News poll reportedly puts Trump’s approval rating at just 36%, with 70% of Americans disapproving of his handling of the economy.

Russia expert Angela Stent, who previously served as a senior intelligence analyst during the George W. Bush administration, suggests that Trump may be preparing Zelensky to become his political scapegoat. If Republicans suffer serious losses in November, Trump could blame Ukraine for high diesel prices and demand Zelensky’s departure.

But Americans struggling with their own economic problems are unlikely to embrace demands for Ukraine to remove its president. And Trump knows that Russian diesel, even if delivered, cannot arrive quickly enough to rescue Republicans before November 3.

This raises an even darker possibility, one that Susan B. Glasser leaves hanging over the entire discussion.

What if Trump is returning to Putin not because he believes it will help Republicans win the midterm elections, but because he genuinely wants Russia to win the war?

That is the question Americans—and the entire democratic world—must confront.

等々力渓谷公園
等々力渓谷、武蔵野台地の南端に位置する延長約１kmの渓谷です。谷沢川が多摩川と合流する手前で、多摩川が形成した河岸段丘、いわゆる国分寺崖線の浸食によってできた、東京都内でもめずらしい渓谷として知られています。
 
「等々力」の地名は、渓谷内の「不動の滝」の音が響き渡り「轟いた」ところからついた、との言い伝えがあります。滝の上部には、平安時代に役の行者の霊場とされた等々力不動尊があり、かってはこの滝に打たれて行をする修行僧が各地から訪れたといいます。
 
渓谷内には「等々力渓谷第３号横穴古墳」があります。これは谷沢川東斜面の崖に群集している横穴のひとつで、古墳時代の末期から奈良時代のものと推定されています。－－－－

Many people take their children to Todoroki Valley because a walk through it offers a wide variety of educational experiences, from observing aquatic life and wetland plants to studying the valley’s geological strata and learning about Japanese history through ancient tunnel tombs.
Todoroki Valley Park
Todoroki Valley is a roughly one-kilometer-long ravine located at the southern edge of the Musashino Plateau. Just before the Yazawa River merges with the Tama River, it passes through an area eroded by the Kokubunji Cliffline—a river terrace formed by the Tama River. This makes Todoroki famous as a rare and unique valley within the Tokyo metropolitan area.
According to local legend, the name "Todoroki" comes from the word todoroita (roared/thundered), describing how the sound of the Fudo Waterfall echoed throughout the valley. Situated above the waterfall is Todoroki Fudoson Temple, which was established as a sacred site by En no Gyoja during the Heian period. It is said that Buddhist monks from various regions once traveled here to practice ascetic training under the cascading water.
Inside the valley lies the "Todoroki Valley No. 3 Tunnel Tomb" (Yokoana Kofun). This is one of a cluster of side-chamber tombs built into the cliff on the eastern slope of the Yazawa River, and is estimated to date from the late Kofun period to the Nara period.
— From the inscription on the stone monument in Todoroki Valley

After a declaration of the type, in the rest of this chap., in the type are described two things, the beast (of whom chap. 13), in verse 3, and the woman that sitteth upon the beast, verses 4, 5, 6. The beast in process of time hath gotten somewhat more than was expressed in the former vision. First in that it is not read before that he was appareled in scarlet, a robe imperial and of triumph. Secondly, in that this is full of names of blasphemy: the other carried the name of blasphemy only in his head. So God did teach that this beast is much increased in impiety and injustice and doth in this last age, triumph in both these more insolently and proudly than ever before.
Revelation 17:3 A scarlet color, that is, with a red and purple garment: and surely it was not without cause that the Romish clergy were so much delighted with this color.
Revelation 17:4 That harlot, the spiritual Babylon, which is Rome. She is described by her attire, profession and deeds.
Revelation 17:4 In attire most glorious, triumphant, most rich, and most gorgeous.
Revelation 17:4 In profession, the nourisher of all, in this verse, and teaching her mysteries unto all, verse 5, setting forth all things most magnificently: but indeed most pernicious besotting miserable men with her cup, and bringing upon them a deadly giddiness.
Revelation 17:5 Deceiving with the title of religion, and public inscription of mystery: which the beast in times past did not bear.
Revelation 17:5 An exposition: in which S. John declareth what manner of woman this is.
Revelation 17:6 In manner of deeds: She is red with blood, and sheddeth it most licentiously, and therefore is colored with the blood of the Saints, as on the contrary part. Christ is set forth imbrued with the blood of his enemies; Isa. 3:1.
Revelation 17:6 A passage unto the second part of this chapter, by occasion given of S. John, as the words of the Angel do show, in the next verse.
Revelation 17:7 The second part or place, as I said, verse 1. The narration of the vision, promised in this verse, and delivered in the verse following. Now there is delivered first a narration of the beast and his story, unto verse 14. After, of the harlot, unto the end of the chap.
Revelation 17:8 The story of the beast hath a triple description of him. The first is a distinction of this beast from all that ever hath been at any time: which distinction is contained in this verse: The second is a delineation or painting out of the beast by things present, by which he might even at that time be known of the godly, and this delineation is according to his heads, verses 2, 10, 11. The third is an historical foretelling of things to come, and to be done by him: and these are ascribed unto his horns, verses 12, 13, 14. This beast is that Empire of Rome, of which I spake, chap. 13:11, according to the mutations and changes whereof which then had already happened, the holy Ghost hath distinguished and set out the same. The Apostle distinguisheth this beast from all others in these words. The beast which thou sawest, was and is not. For so I expound the words of the Apostle for evidence’s sake as I will further declare in the notes following.
Revelation 17:8 The meaning is, that beast which thou sawest before (Rev. 13:1) and which yet thou hast now seen, was, (I say was) even from Julius Caesar in respect of beginning, rising up, station, glory, dominion, manner and stock, from the house of Julius: and yet is not now the same, if thou look unto the house and stock for the dominion of this family was translated unto another, after the death of Nero from the other unto a third, from a third unto a fourth, and so forth was varied and altered by innumerable changes. Finally, the Empire is one, as it were one beast: but exceedingly varied by kindreds, families, and persons. It was therefore (saith S. John) in the kindred or house of Julius: and now it is not in that kindred, but translated unto another.
Revelation 17:8 As if he should say, Also the same that is, shall shortly not be: but shall ascend out of the depth, or out of the sea (as was said, Rev. 13:1) that is, shall be a new stock from amongst the nations without difference, and shall in the same state go unto destruction or ruin, and perish: and so shall successively new Princes or Emperors come and go, arise and fall, the body of the beast remaining still, but tossed with so many and often alterations, as no man can but marvel that this beast was able to stand and hold out, in so many mutations. Verily no Empire that ever was tossed with so many changes, and as it were with so many tempests of the sea, ever continued so long.
Revelation 17:8 That is as many as have not learned the providence of God, according to the faith of the Saints, shall marvel at these grievous and often changes when they shall consider, the selfsame beast, which is the Roman Empire, to have been, not to be, and to be and still molested with perpetual mutation, and yet in the same to stand and continue. This in mine opinion is the most simple exposition of this place, and confirmed by the event of the things themselves. Although by the last change also, by which the Empire, that before was civil became Ecclesiastical, is not obscurely signified by these words: of which two, the first exercised cruelty upon the bodies of the saints: the other also upon their souls: the first by human order and policy, the other under the color of the law of God, and of Religion, raged and imbrued itself with the blood of the godly.
Revelation 17:9 An exhortation preparing unto audience, by the same argument, with that of Christ: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Wherefore, for mine own part, I had rather read in this place, Let there be here a mind, etc. So the Angel passeth fully unto the second place of this description.
Revelation 17:9 Very children know what that seven hilled city is, which is so much spoken of, and whereof Virgil thus reporteth, And compasseth seven towers in one wall: that city it is, which when John wrote these things had rule over the kings of the earth: It was and is not, and yet it remaineth this day, but it is declining to destruction.
Revelation 17:9 This is the painting out of the beast by things present (as I said before) whereby S. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. And here it is worthy to be observed, that one type hath sometimes two or more applications, as seemeth good unto the holy Ghost to express either one thing by divers types, or divers things by one type. So I noted before, of the seven spirits, Rev. 1:4. Now this woman that sitteth upon seven hills, is the city of Rome, called in times past of the Greeks, … i. of seven tops or crests, and of Varro, septiceps, i. of her seven heads (as here) of seven heads, and of others, septicollis, i. standing upon seven hills.
Revelation 17:9 The beginning of these Kings or Emperors is almost the same with the beginning of the Church of Christ, which I showed before, Rev. 11:1. Namely from the year 35, after the passion of Christ, what time the Temple and Church of the Jews was overthrown. In which year it came to pass by the providence of God that that saying The beast was and is not, was fulfilled before that the destruction of the Jews immediately following came to pass. That was the year from the building of the city of Rome, 109, from which year S. John both numbered the Emperors which hitherto hath been, when he wrote these things, and foretelleth two others next to come: and that with this purpose, that when this particular prediction of foretelling of things to come, should take effect the truth of all other predictions in the Church might be the more confirmed. Which sign God of old mentioned this in the Law, Deut. 18, and Jeremiah confirmeth, Jer. 28:8.
Revelation 17:10 Whose names are these: the first, Servius Sulpicius Galba, who was the seventh Emperor of the people of Rome, the second Marcus Salvius Otho, the third Aulus Vitellius, the fourth, Titus Flavius Vespasianus, the fifth, Titus Vespasianus his son of his own name.
Revelation 17:10 Flavius Domitian son of the first Vespasian. For in the latter end of his days S. John wrote these things, as witnesseth Irenaus, Lib. 5 adversus hareses.
Revelation 17:10 Nerua. The Empire being now translated from the family of Flavius. This man reigned only one year, four months, and nine days, as the history writers do tell.
Revelation 17:11 This is spoken by the figure synecdoche, as much to say as that head of the beast which was and is not, because it is cut off, and Nerua in so short time extinguished. How many heads there were, so many beasts there seemed to be in one. See the like speech in Rev. 13.3
Revelation 17:11 Nerua Traianus, who himself in divers respects is called here the seventh and the eighth.
Revelation 17:11 Though in number and order of succession he be the eighth, yet he is reckoned together with one of these heads, because Nerua and he were one head. For this man obtained authority together with Nerua, and was Consul with him, when Nerua left his life.
Revelation 17:11 Namely, to molest with persecutions the Churches of Christ, as the histories do accord, and I have briefly noted, Rev. 2:10.
Revelation 17:12 The third place of this description as I said, verse 18, is a prophetical prediction of things to come which the beast should do, as in the words following S. John doth not obscurely signify, saying, which have not yet received the kingdom, etc. For there is an Antithesis or opposition between these kings, and those that went before. And first the persons are described, in this verse, then their deeds in the two verses following.
Revelation 17:12 That is, arising with their kingdoms out of the Roman beast: at such time as that political Empire began by the craft of the Popes greatly to fall.
Revelation 17:12 Namely, with the second beast whom we called before a false prophet, which beast, ascending out of the earth got unto himself all the authority and power of the first beast, and exerciseth the same before his face, as was said, Rev. 14:11, 12. For when the political Empire of the West began to bow downwards, there both arose those ten kings, and the second beast took the opportunity offered to usurp unto himself all the power of the former beast. These kings long ago, many have numbered and described to be ten and a great part of the events plainly testifieth the same in this our age.
Revelation 17:13 That is, by consent and agreement, that they may conspire with the beast, and depend upon his beck. Their story is divided into three parts, counsels, acts, and events. The counselors some of them consist in communicating of judgments and affections: and some in communicating of power, which they are said to have given unto this beast in this verse.
Revelation 17:14 With Christ and his Church, as the reason following doth declare, and here are mentioned the facts and the events which followed for Christ’s sake, and for the grace of God the Father towards those that are called, elected, and are his faithful ones in Christ.
Revelation 17:15 This is the other member of the narration as I said verse 7, belonging unto the harlot, showed in the vision, verse 3. In this history of the harlot, these 3 things are distinctly propounded, what is her magnificence in this verse, what is her fall, and by whom it shall happen unto her, in the two verses following: and lastly, who that harlot is, in the last verse. This place which by order of nature should have been the first, is therefore made the last, because it was more fit to be joined with the next Chap.
Revelation 17:15 That is, as unconstant and variable as the waters. Upon this foundation sitteth this harlot as Queen, a vain person upon that which is vain.
Revelation 17:16 The ten Kings as verse 12. The accomplishment of this fact and event, is daily increased in this our age by the singular providence and most mighty government of God. Wherefore the facts are propounded in this verse, and the cause of them in the verses following.
Revelation 17:17 A reason rendered from the chief efficient cause, which is the providence of God, by which alone S. John by inversion of order affirmeth to have come to pass, both that the Kings should execute upon the harlot, that which pleased God, and which he declared in the verse next beforegoing: and also that by one consent and counsel, they should give their kingdom unto the beast, etc., verses 13, 14. For as these being blinded have before depended upon the beck of the beast that lifteth up the harlot, so it is said that afterward it shall come to pass, that they shall turn back, and shall fall away from her when their hearts shall be turned into better state by the grace and mercy of God.
Revelation 17:18 That is, Rome that great City, or only City (as Justinian calleth it) the King and head whereof was then the Emperor, but now the Pope, since that the condition of the beast was changed.

The Boon He Sought for Humanity

As his earthly journey neared its end, the Mother offered Sastry a boon.

He asked that a Sanskrit verse he composed be inscribed on a stone tablet at her Bala Tripura Sundari temple, so that devotees who read it with heartfelt prayer might receive her grace.

The tablet is said to be at Ganganampeta, Tenali.

Sastry passed away on 10 December 1990. 
His family recounts that a divine form appeared in the cremation flames and rose into the sky. The phenomenon was reportedly covered by Andhra Bhoomi in 1991.

Verily no Empire that ever was tossed with so many changes, and as it were with so many tempests of the sea, ever continued so long.
Revelation 17:8 That is as many as have not learned the providence of God, according to the faith of the Saints, shall marvel at these grievous and often changes when they shall consider, the selfsame beast, which is the Roman Empire, to have been, not to be, and to be and still molested with perpetual mutation, and yet in the same to stand and continue. This in mine opinion is the most simple exposition of this place, and confirmed by the event of the things themselves. Although by the last change also, by which the Empire, that before was civil became Ecclesiastical, is not obscurely signified by these words: of which two, the first exercised cruelty upon the bodies of the saints: the other also upon their souls: the first by human order and policy, the other under the color of the law of God, and of Religion, raged and imbrued itself with the blood of the godly.
Revelation 17:9 An exhortation preparing unto audience, by the same argument, with that of Christ: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Wherefore, for mine own part, I had rather read in this place, Let there be here a mind, etc. So the Angel passeth fully unto the second place of this description.
Revelation 17:9 Very children know what that seven hilled city is, which is so much spoken of, and whereof Virgil thus reporteth, And compasseth seven towers in one wall: that city it is, which when John wrote these things had rule over the kings of the earth: It was and is not, and yet it remaineth this day, but it is declining to destruction.
Revelation 17:9 This is the painting out of the beast by things present (as I said before) whereby S. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. And here it is worthy to be observed, that one type hath sometimes two or more applications, as seemeth good unto the holy Ghost to express either one thing by divers types, or divers things by one type. So I noted before, of the seven spirits, Rev. 1:4. Now this woman that sitteth upon seven hills, is the city of Rome, called in times past of the Greeks, … i. of seven tops or crests, and of Varro, septiceps, i. of her seven heads (as here) of seven heads, and of others, septicollis, i. standing upon seven hills.
Revelation 17:9 The beginning of these Kings or Emperors is almost the same with the beginning of the Church of Christ, which I showed before, Rev. 11:1. Namely from the year 35, after the passion of Christ, what time the Temple and Church of the Jews was overthrown. In which year it came to pass by the providence of God that that saying The beast was and is not, was fulfilled before that the destruction of the Jews immediately following came to pass. That was the year from the building of the city of Rome, 109, from which year S. John both numbered the Emperors which hitherto hath been, when he wrote these things, and foretelleth two others next to come: and that with this purpose, that when this particular prediction of foretelling of things to come, should take effect the truth of all other predictions in the Church might be the more confirmed. Which sign God of old mentioned this in the Law, Deut. 18, and Jeremiah confirmeth, Jer. 28:8.
Revelation 17:10 Whose names are these: the first, Servius Sulpicius Galba, who was the seventh Emperor of the people of Rome, the second Marcus Salvius Otho, the third Aulus Vitellius, the fourth, Titus Flavius Vespasianus, the fifth, Titus Vespasianus his son of his own name.
Revelation 17:10 Flavius Domitian son of the first Vespasian. For in the latter end of his days S. John wrote these things, as witnesseth Irenaus, Lib. 5 adversus hareses.
Revelation 17:10 Nerua. The Empire being now translated from the family of Flavius. This man reigned only one year, four months, and nine days, as the history writers do tell.
Revelation 17:11 This is spoken by the figure synecdoche, as much to say as that head of the beast which was and is not, because it is cut off, and Nerua in so short time extinguished. How many heads there were, so many beasts there seemed to be in one. See the like speech in Rev. 13.3
Revelation 17:11 Nerua Traianus, who himself in divers respects is called here the seventh and the eighth.
Revelation 17:11 Though in number and order of succession he be the eighth, yet he is reckoned together with one of these heads, because Nerua and he were one head. For this man obtained authority together with Nerua, and was Consul with him, when Nerua left his life.
Revelation 17:11 Namely, to molest with persecutions the Churches of Christ, as the histories do accord, and I have briefly noted, Rev. 2:10.
Revelation 17:12 The third place of this description as I said, verse 18, is a prophetical prediction of things to come which the beast should do, as in the words following S. John doth not obscurely signify, saying, which have not yet received the kingdom, etc. For there is an Antithesis or opposition between these kings, and those that went before. And first the persons are described, in this verse, then their deeds in the two verses following.
Revelation 17:12 That is, arising with their kingdoms out of the Roman beast: at such time as that political Empire began by the craft of the Popes greatly to fall.
Revelation 17:12 Namely, with the second beast whom we called before a false prophet, which beast, ascending out of the earth got unto himself all the authority and power of the first beast, and exerciseth the same before his face, as was said, Rev. 14:11, 12. For when the political Empire of the West began to bow downwards, there both arose those ten kings, and the second beast took the opportunity offered to usurp unto himself all the power of the former beast. These kings long ago, many have numbered and described to be ten and a great part of the events plainly testifieth the same in this our age.
Revelation 17:13 That is, by consent and agreement, that they may conspire with the beast, and depend upon his beck. Their story is divided into three parts, counsels, acts, and events. The counselors some of them consist in communicating of judgments and affections: and some in communicating of power, which they are said to have given unto this beast in this verse.
Revelation 17:14 With Christ and his Church, as the reason following doth declare, and here are mentioned the facts and the events which followed for Christ’s sake, and for the grace of God the Father towards those that are called, elected, and are his faithful ones in Christ.
Revelation 17:15 This is the other member of the narration as I said verse 7, belonging unto the harlot, showed in the vision, verse 3. In this history of the harlot, these 3 things are distinctly propounded, what is her magnificence in this verse, what is her fall, and by whom it shall happen unto her, in the two verses following: and lastly, who that harlot is, in the last verse. This place which by order of nature should have been the first, is therefore made the last, because it was more fit to be joined with the next Chap.
Revelation 17:15 That is, as unconstant and variable as the waters. Upon this foundation sitteth this harlot as Queen, a vain person upon that which is vain.
Revelation 17:16 The ten Kings as verse 12. The accomplishment of this fact and event, is daily increased in this our age by the singular providence and most mighty government of God. Wherefore the facts are propounded in this verse, and the cause of them in the verses following.
Revelation 17:17 A reason rendered from the chief efficient cause, which is the providence of God, by which alone S. John by inversion of order affirmeth to have come to pass, both that the Kings should execute upon the harlot, that which pleased God, and which he declared in the verse next beforegoing: and also that by one consent and counsel, they should give their kingdom unto the beast, etc., verses 13, 14. For as these being blinded have before depended upon the beck of the beast that lifteth up the harlot, so it is said that afterward it shall come to pass, that they shall turn back, and shall fall away from her when their hearts shall be turned into better state by the grace and mercy of God.
Revelation 17:18 That is, Rome that great City, or only City (as Justinian calleth it) the King and head whereof was then the Emperor, but now the Pope, since that the condition of the beast was changed.

The magnificent Vijaya Vitthala Temple stands as a remarkable testament to the artistic brilliance, architectural excellence, and cultural richness of the Vijayanagara Empire.

The intricate patterns and distinctive carvings found on its ancient granite surfaces offer a fascinating glimpse into the craftsmanship and artistic traditions of a bygone era. These enduring details invite us to appreciate the creativity, dedication, and aesthetic sensibilities of the artisans who contributed to India's extraordinary architectural heritage.

Historic Hampi flourished as an important centre of religious devotion, artistic expression, and cultural life. The temple's remarkable architectural features reflect the sophistication and grandeur of the civilization that shaped this historic landscape.

Although centuries of exposure have weathered many stone surfaces, their enduring beauty continues to inspire admiration, connecting modern generations with the artistic achievements of the past.

Recognized as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi, this extraordinary monument preserves an invaluable legacy of India's history, architecture, and cultural identity.

Every stone echoes the wisdom of generations, every carving reflects the brilliance of human creativity, and every architectural detail reminds us that true heritage transcends the boundaries of time.

📍 India's heritage is not merely a memory of the past; it is a timeless legacy that continues to enlighten, inspire, and unite generations.

So he repeatedly (5x) said that we need to eat his flesh and drink his blood, and then offered up bread and wine and said they are his body and blood, but those things were not meant to be understood together?

Jesus was speaking to first century Jews who understood worship to be when you took a sacrifice to the Temple and shared a meal with God.  They knew you could take unleavened loaves to the temple to offer God a thanksgiving offering (Leviticus 7:12).  They knew full well about Melchizedek, the priest king whose order was signified by offering bread and wine to God (Genesis 14:18, Psalm 110:4).  They had heard St John the Baptist call Jesus the Lamb of God, in reference to the Passover lamb that was sacrificed and eaten in a meal shared with God.  

Jesus didn’t have to say “hey guys, this is a sacrifice by the way.”

That’s like me saying “he ran into the end zone for a touchdown” and you saying “but we don’t know what sport you were talking about because you didn’t say it was football.”

Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh: Ravan village in Nateran tehsil observes a unique Dussehra tradition, with no Ravana effigy burning, as villagers worship him as their village deity, affectionately known as Ravan Baba. An ancient Parmar-era temple houses a 12-foot reclining idol, where daily prayers and aarti are performed. Villagers seek Ravan Baba’s blessings before weddings, religious ceremonies and new vehicle purchases, with the first wedding invitation offered to him. On Dussehra, the village hosts Ramayana recitations, devotional singing and a grand community feast, drawing devotees from Vidisha, Bhopal and nearby areas.

text:
ACC coaching hot seats: Norvell stays No. 1; O’Brien gets relief, Belichick gains ground

Mike Norvell remains the ACC football coach facing the greatest pressure after Florida State’s double-overtime loss at Miami dropped the Seminoles below .500. Boston College’s Bill O’Brien earned needed breathing room by beating Pitt, while North Carolina’s Bill Belichick strengthened his position with a second consecutive conference road victory, this time over rival Duke. 

The most consequential situations remain Florida State, NC State, Boston College and Syracuse. Clemson’s Dabo Swinney faces substantial scrutiny over his program’s direction, although his championship record makes his job-security situation different from those of the coaches above him.

These rankings are editorial assessments of job security, weighing results, opponent strength, recent trajectory, tenure and program expectations. They do not indicate that schools have decided to dismiss their coaches. Reported concerns about a coach’s future are distinguished below from our assessment.

All 17 ACC coaches: Hottest seat to coolest

 The coaches facing the most consequential finishes

1. Mike Norvell — Florida State

The Miami performance helps his argument. The result keeps him first.

Florida State pushed unbeaten Miami into double overtime before losing 43–35. That is a considerably more encouraging showing than the previous week’s decisive defeat at Louisville, and opponent strength must count when evaluating the Seminoles. Nevertheless, Florida State enters its remaining schedule needing three victories to reach six wins.

Norvell’s pressure predates this season. When Florida State announced his retention last November, President Richard McCullough said that “success must be achieved.” That institutional demand makes another season spent struggling toward bowl eligibility particularly consequential. 

Assessment: The clearest hot seat in the conference. A competitive rivalry loss provides evidence of effort and capability, but sustained winning remains the strongest argument for retaining him.

What would help: A winning finish, bowl eligibility and fewer games in which a promising position becomes another defeat.

2. Dave Doeren — NC State

An idle weekend moves Doeren up because O’Brien produced a meaningful win.

NC State had no Oct. 17 game, leaving the 38–14 home loss to Wake Forest as its most recent result. That defeat followed a victory over Louisville, illustrating the central question surrounding this team: Can the Wolfpack sustain progress against conference opponents? 

Doeren’s long tenure and history of competitive teams provide protection. However, the pressure is supported by reporting beyond fan frustration. Sports Illustrated identified his season as consequential and described renewed questions about whether NC State should make a change if results disappointed. 

Assessment: Serious pressure, with the remaining schedule carrying substantial weight. His rise from third to second reflects Boston College’s improvement more than a new development in Raleigh.

What would help: A strong closing stretch that makes the Louisville victory representative of the team’s ability.

3. Bill O’Brien — Boston College

The Pitt victory is precisely the kind of result his case needed.

Boston College defeated Pitt 27–21, securing its first ACC victory and returning to .500. Beating a team that entered with five wins carries more weight than merely improving the record against a lesser opponent.

That earns O’Brien a one-place drop toward the cooler end of the rankings. It also changes the discussion from whether Boston College can win a conference game to whether the Eagles can build a credible postseason push.

His position still requires attention. September reporting identified O’Brien’s situation as uncertain and emphasized the difficult schedule facing the Eagles. One victory improves that picture without resolving the full season.

Assessment: Still hot, but with tangible relief.

What would help: Additional ACC victories and a finish that establishes clear improvement.

4. Fran Brown — Syracuse

The absence of conference victories is becoming increasingly difficult to overcome.

Syracuse lost 34–26 to Louisville, extending its winless ACC start to four games. The margin shows a competitive game, but another opportunity to change the conference record passed without a victory. 

Brown’s situation also has an administrative dimension. Sports Illustrated reported in September that he needed to demonstrate progress to a new athletic director, while noting that an expensive buyout complicated any potential change. 

Assessment: Pressure mounting. Brown stays fourth because the coaches above him have stronger established hot-seat cases, but Syracuse’s direction remains concerning.

What would help: Conference wins that demonstrate improvement in execution and restore confidence in the program’s trajectory.

5. Dabo Swinney — Clemson

A comfortable victory stabilizes the season without settling the larger questions.

Clemson beat Charleston Southern 37–0. The Tigers handled the assignment, but a victory over an FCS opponent provides limited evidence about their ability to compete with the strongest teams on their schedule. 

Swinney’s ranking reflects scrutiny of Clemson’s recent direction and performances in major games. His championship history remains a substantial reason to distinguish that scrutiny from the more immediate concerns at Florida State.

Assessment: Significant pressure to restore Clemson’s standing, with stronger institutional protection than most coaches near the top.

What would help: Convincing performances against quality ACC opposition.

 6. Brent Key — Georgia Tech

The relief from beating Duke lasted one week.

Georgia Tech followed its victory over Duke with a 34–24 loss at Virginia Tech. Losing on the road to a winning opponent is understandable in isolation. The cumulative problem is that the Yellow Jackets have lost four of their first six games. 

Key moves ahead of Belichick because their teams are heading in different directions. This placement reflects concern about Tech’s season, rather than verified evidence that administrators are preparing a coaching change.

Assessment: Warming, with a meaningful need to recover.

What would help: Consecutive victories and a credible route to bowl eligibility.

7. Bill Belichick — North Carolina

Few coaches on this list have improved their position more over the past two weeks.

North Carolina followed its victory at Pitt by beating Duke 24–20 in Durham and reclaiming the Victory Bell. Jaylen McGill supplied the decisive touchdown, and Kenton Dopson III intercepted a pass with 14 seconds remaining to preserve the victory. 

Winning consecutive ACC road games gives Belichick a much stronger performance-based case. The Duke victory also carries the additional importance of a rivalry result.

He remains in the upper half because expectations surrounding his tenure are substantial. However, his current position is considerably cooler than it was in September.

Assessment: Cooling meaningfully. The recent results support confidence in improvement.

What would help: Maintaining that consistency and converting the strong first half into a postseason appearance.

Coaches with concerns, but less immediate danger

8. Pat Narduzzi — Pitt

Two consecutive losses bring the questions back.

Pitt’s 27–21 defeat at Boston College followed its home loss to North Carolina. The Panthers’ unbeaten start has become a season requiring a response. 

Narduzzi rises two places because recent results intersect with an existing concern. Sports Illustrated’s September assessment highlighted Pitt’s tendency to lose momentum later in seasons and suggested another disappointing finish could prompt administrative discussions. 

Assessment: Renewed scrutiny, although his team has built a stronger record than those of most coaches ranked above him.

What would help: A convincing finish that prevents the recent defeats from becoming a prolonged slide.

9. Jeff Brohm — Louisville

Consecutive victories have improved his position.

Louisville followed its win over Florida State with a 34–26 road victory at Syracuse. That provides evidence of recovery after an uneven opening stretch. 

Brohm drops one place toward safety. His team still has work to do, but the current trend supports greater confidence.

Assessment: Moderate performance pressure; the evidence for immediate job danger is limited.

What would help: Sustaining the winning run against stronger opponents.

10. Tony Elliott — Virginia

The SMU loss creates a competitive concern more than a job-security crisis.

Virginia lost 23–13 at SMU. A road defeat against a team with only one loss deserves context, even as the Cavaliers need to regain momentum. 

Elliott moves one place cooler because Narduzzi’s circumstances have become more concerning. That movement does not imply that Virginia’s defeat helped Elliott.

Assessment: Relatively secure, with pressure to produce a solid finish.

11. Tosh Lupoi — California

The Wake Forest defeat was severe, but patience remains appropriate.

Cal lost 41–7 at home to Wake Forest. The margin raises clear questions about the Bears’ competitiveness, particularly after their victory over Virginia Tech the previous week. 

For a first-year coach, however, one difficult performance should carry less job-security weight than a multiyear pattern of disappointing results.

Assessment: Low immediate risk. The priority is showing a response and establishing a foundation for improvement.

12. Tavita Pritchard — Stanford

Stanford supplied a needed response against Elon.

The Cardinal won 34–7, with Micah Ford scoring four touchdowns. It was a useful recovery following the heavy defeat at Notre Dame, although the level of opposition limits how much the win changes the broader evaluation. 

Pritchard moves one place cooler. As a first-year coach, he should be evaluated primarily on the development of the program and its ability to become more competitive.

Assessment: Low immediate risk, with continued rebuilding work ahead.

The coolest seats

13. James Franklin — Virginia Tech

The Hokies interrupted their losing streak.

Virginia Tech beat Georgia Tech 34–24, providing a timely recovery after consecutive defeats. Franklin’s first season continues to offer a solid foundation despite those setbacks. 

Assessment: Secure. Expectations will rise with success, but current results provide little basis for a serious hot-seat argument.

14. Rhett Lashlee — SMU

The Mustangs keep strengthening their position.

SMU’s 23–13 victory over Virginia added another conference win and kept the Mustangs firmly among the ACC’s leading teams. 

Assessment: Secure. Lashlee’s immediate challenge is maintaining contention and meeting rising expectations.

5. Manny Diaz — Duke

The rivalry defeat hurts, but two close losses should not overwhelm the broader assessment.

Duke’s loss to North Carolina followed its narrow defeat at Georgia Tech. Consecutive conference setbacks have reduced the margin for error, and losing the Victory Bell adds emotional weight. 

Those outcomes warrant scrutiny of how Duke finishes close games. They provide limited grounds for a major change in Diaz’s job-security ranking.

Assessment: Very secure, with an immediate need to stabilize results.

16. Jake Dickert — Wake Forest

Wake’s season continues to strengthen his standing.

The Demon Deacons secured bowl eligibility with their 41–7 victory at Cal. Dickert also appeared on the Dodd Trophy’s midseason watchlist, providing recognition of the season’s coaching performance. 

Assessment: Among the conference’s safest coaches. Wake’s results support growing confidence in his tenure.

17. Mario Cristobal — Miami

The Hurricanes survived a major test and remain unbeaten.

Miami’s 43–35 double-overtime victory over Florida State preserved its perfect record. The close margin supplies material for improvement, but winning a difficult rivalry game further strengthens Cristobal’s position. 

Assessment: Coolest seat in the ACC. Championship expectations are high, and his team continues to meet the most fundamental requirement: winning.

The next stretch matters most for Norvell, Doeren, O’Brien and Brown. O’Brien has supplied a timely victory; Doeren needs a response after the Wake Forest defeat; Brown needs conference wins; and Norvell needs the competitiveness shown against Miami to produce victories. Belichick has made the strongest recent move toward security, with consecutive road wins giving his program a clearer case for progress.

text:
Why US Stocks Could Go Nowhere for Years
Imagine sitting at the White House economic policy table. Three problems are in front of you: technology companies want to keep building data centers, voters want a lower cost of living, and the Treasury needs to keep selling debt.

You want AI investment to continue. It supports growth, jobs, and technological leadership. You also want lower interest rates, because households, businesses, and the government all find borrowing expensive. Yet the faster investment expands, the more pressure it puts on power, equipment, and capital. Cut rates too aggressively, and bond investors may start worrying about inflation again.

Move to the Federal Reserve, and the trade-offs remain. You can believe AI will raise productivity without treating tomorrow's promised cost savings as an answer to today's inflation. You need a functioning financial system, but that does not require protecting every elevated valuation.

Policymakers in both buildings need time. That is why I think US stocks could face years of disappointing returns: AI's success has yet to deliver broad enough economic gains to validate the expectations embedded in asset prices, while evidence of failure remains too limited to overturn the entire investment cycle.

Rallies run into inflation and debt constraints. Selloffs run into real demand, corporate cash flow, and potential policy support. Repeated repricing becomes more plausible than a durable move in one direction.

Washington wants the buildout to continue

This tension is already visible in policy.

In March 2026, the White House secured commitments from major technology companies to bear the costs of additional power generation and related grid upgrades for data centers, with the aim of protecting households from higher electricity bills. The political objective was straightforward: keep building AI infrastructure while containing the cost to voters.

But assigning the bill does not instantly produce another transformer, skilled electrician, or power plant. If companies absorb more of the cost, investment returns come under pressure. If households absorb it, purchasing power and political support suffer. Someone has to pay for scarce resources.

In September, the Fed acknowledged strong productivity growth and robust capital investment while raising its policy rate to 3.75%–4.00%. September CPI, released in October, showed prices up 3.7% from a year earlier. That offered little comfort to investors counting on rapid easing.

The sequence matters. AI first buys equipment, builds facilities, and competes for energy. Broader efficiency gains arrive as businesses redesign how they operate. The spending increases demand before the full productivity dividend expands supply.

The White House wants to make that future dividend possible. The Fed has to manage the prices being paid in the meantime. The same AI development can therefore improve a technology company's revenue outlook and delay the rate cuts investors want.

For assets already priced for years of growth, good news does not automatically justify a higher valuation.

Earnings need to catch up with promises

From the White House's perspective, AI's most valuable outcome is an economy that produces more saleable goods and services with the same resources. That would support profits, household incomes, and the tax base. Spending more on data centers is only an input into that process.

Productivity is already improving. US nonfarm business labor productivity rose 2.2% year over year in the second quarter. The next question is whether those gains can spread and persist, improving businesses beyond the AI sector quickly enough to justify the investment and valuations already committed.

Faster coding is a beginning. Changes to procurement, logistics, healthcare, manufacturing, sales, and management are what gradually reshape costs across the economy. Models can improve every month. Organizations, infrastructure, and working practices rarely move at the same speed.

Federal borrowing makes the waiting expensive. In its early October estimate, the Congressional Budget Office put the fiscal 2026 deficit at almost $2 trillion. The Treasury must finance new borrowing while refinancing maturing debt. The White House would welcome cheaper funding, but a lower Fed policy rate does not guarantee lower long-term Treasury yields.

Bond investors still price inflation, the future path of rates, and the risks of holding long-duration debt. If they think easing will tolerate more inflation, long yields may refuse to follow short rates down. Larger deficits used to support demand can also raise the return investors require.

For expensive equities, that means distant profits continue to be discounted at a demanding rate.

A sustained advance therefore needs a credible path toward broader earnings growth, easing inflation pressure, and a more manageable fiscal trajectory. The federal debt does not have to disappear. Investors do need to believe that income and productive capacity can increasingly support the obligations being accumulated.

Until that path becomes clearer, rallies risk spending the productivity dividend before it arrives. Rising asset prices can then reinforce wealth effects and investment, supporting demand and bringing the constraints back sooner.

An AI bust needs its own dark-fiber reckoning

Policymakers also need more than a large investment number to conclude that the entire buildout is a mistake.

The telecom industry showed what a genuine breakdown looked like around 2000. Companies laid vast amounts of long-haul fiber. Paying demand failed to grow as fast as builders had expected, while construction and technological advances rapidly expanded transmission capacity.

The internet kept growing. Customers gained cheaper communications. Some of the companies financing the infrastructure saw their capital returns destroyed.

Dark fiber became a symbol of that overbuild. For lenders and shareholders, the central issue was whether assets could earn enough, soon enough, to repay the capital committed to them. Eventual usefulness could not meet an approaching debt payment.

An AI version would likewise show up in investment returns: additional capacity persistently selling at prices too low to cover its costs, customers cutting or renegotiating purchases, falling equipment resale values, and increasingly difficult refinancing. As these pressures reinforce one another, isolated project failures can become an industry-wide contraction.

GPUs face an especially unforgiving timetable. New chips improve energy efficiency and cost per task. Older equipment can lose economic competitiveness while its owners wait for demand to catch up. A data center can remain busy while its shareholders fail to recover their original investment.

Markets will anticipate that deterioration. They do not need to wait for facilities to close. But a sustained, 2000-style collapse along the AI investment chain requires growing conviction that the revenue generated by additional capacity cannot justify continued expansion.

Until that conviction strengthens, the established cash flows of large technology companies, actual customer spending, and genuine technical progress will keep challenging the case for wholesale failure. Individual borrowers can get into trouble well before the industry loses its economic value.

That creates a frustrating middle ground: AI is useful enough to keep construction going, while the gains spread too slowly to justify ever-higher valuations.

Policy can buy time while shareholders pay for it

In this situation, the White House has reason to accelerate power supply, permitting, and infrastructure delivery. The Fed must adjust to inflation, employment, and financial conditions.

Their responsibilities differ. Neither is required to defend a particular stock index level. Both, however, have reason to avoid a sudden collapse in financing for viable projects or a breakdown in markets that damages the wider economy.

That makes an adjustment in stages plausible. When activity overheats, financing costs and policy constraints restrain expansion. When growth weakens and inflation eases, room for monetary easing returns. If credit markets malfunction, liquidity tools may come into play. Restoring market functioning does not require restoring yesterday's equity valuations.

Policy could therefore prevent an uncontrolled financial contraction while leaving investors with several years of poor stock returns. Washington gains an adjustment window. The Fed preserves its inflation credibility. Shareholders absorb part of the cost through lower valuation multiples and the passage of time.

Profits do not even have to stop growing.

Suppose an index begins at 30 times earnings. Earnings grow 8% a year for three years, increasing by roughly 26%. Over the same period, its valuation falls to 24 times earnings. The index price ends up almost exactly where it started. Dividends are additional, but much of the operating progress has gone toward absorbing the price investors paid at the beginning.

That is the dead-money scenario: businesses evolve, winners and losers diverge, and stocks experience powerful rallies and painful declines, yet owning assets priced for high expectations produces little reward for the volatility endured.

Every rebound looks like a new bull market. Every correction looks like the start of a crash. Both sides keep mistaking an interim development for the final verdict.

This can last for years because productivity diffusion, power infrastructure, debt refinancing, and investment returns operate on longer timelines than a Fed meeting. Quarterly data can change the market's mood without resolving any of those processes.

The clearest routes out lie in two sets of evidence. One is a broad improvement in earnings and incomes beyond the AI sector, accompanied by easing inflation and fiscal financing pressure. That would strengthen the case that growth can justify valuations.

The other is a persistent deterioration in returns on additional computing capacity, followed by weakening customer commitments and refinancing access. That would force investors to recognize that capital needs to be written down.

Until one path becomes more convincing, treating every rally as the start of a lasting bull market, or every selloff as another 2000, risks committing too early.

For the White House and the Fed, getting the economy through this transition could count as a policy success. For investors, success requires an additional condition: paying a price that leaves room for the wait.

Washington needs time. Shareholders need returns. The next few years may expose just how far apart those two objectives can be.

🏈 THE HANDLE REPORT | MNF MARKET ANALYSIS

Washington Commanders @ San Francisco 49ers

📊 Market: SF -7.5 | Total: 52–52.5

Everybody sees the undefeated 49ers. I’m looking at the situation Washington is walking into. 👀

📉 THE MARKET

🔵 Circa

73% of spread tickets on SF
80% of spread money on SF
92% of ML money on SF

🟢 DraftKings

72% of spread tickets on SF
63% of spread money on SF
93% of ML tickets on SF

Circa opened SF -8, yet we’re sitting at -7.5 despite significant money backing the favorite.

That’s worth paying attention to. The market isn’t forcing bettors to lay a bigger number.

⚔️ THE MATCHUP

PFF strength of schedule:

Washington: 10th
San Francisco: 25th

Washington has faced tougher competition, while SF’s undefeated record has come against a lighter schedule.

The 49ers have the offensive efficiency advantage, no question. But Washington’s offensive line gets a San Francisco defensive front that hasn’t been dominant across the board, and Jayden Daniels’ mobility creates another problem.

🔥 THE SITUATIONAL SPOT

San Francisco is coming off an emotional division win against Seattle.

Washington is coming off a late-game collapse and is fighting to keep its season from slipping away.

One team is undefeated and getting plenty of attention. The other is desperate for a response.

That doesn’t guarantee anything, but the circumstances matter.

📈 THE NUMBERS

My module: SF -8.24
Recent: SF -11.94
Strong: SF -12.20
PFF projection: SF -8.3

The ratings favor San Francisco. I’m not ignoring that.

But power ratings don’t fully capture every situational factor, and the market has already priced SF as a substantial favorite.

🎯 MARKET READ

I’m interested in Washington +7.5 and the ML.

The spread gives us protection in a competitive game, while the moneyline offers an opportunity if Daniels can turn this into a fourth-quarter possession game.

This isn’t about saying Washington is the better team.

It’s about whether an undefeated favorite coming off a big win is being priced too aggressively against a desperate opponent that’s played a tougher schedule.

The 49ers may be the better team. That doesn’t automatically make them the better bet. 🎯

text:
Sea Tow, Dammit Bart, defamation and targeting mega thread. Story time.

All times below are Eastern daylight time in 2026. Video dates are publication times; timestamps inside videos locate the speech, not its recording time. Dates without an exact time do not establish an order within that day.

This follows the sources currently verified. Accusations remain attributed accusations. Questions, slogans, corrections and threats are distinguished. A comment beneath someone’s post does not establish that the publisher endorsed it. Where a direct reply is established, it is identified. Undated original YouTube comments appear separately at the end.

• July 21, 10:13:19 PM: Officer Tatum publishes the original Part 1 of his Warren Hudson interview on YouTube. At 8:20.919, the guest identified as Warren says, “I went with my buddy Bart.” Around 8:27, he recalls asking, “Hey man, can you take your boat out?” He later says, “I rode out there with Bart.” Bart enters this account as a friend bringing a boat.

• July 22, 12:32:52 PM: Boogie THEE LowDown republishes Tatum’s Part 1 on Facebook, about 14 hours 19 minutes after the original YouTube upload. These are separate publications with separate comment sections. At 8:50:42 PM, Facebook user Waverly Wooding writes under Boogie’s copy, “So he was on Barts boat, but he trailered Tim’s boat?” This is the earliest precisely dated written Bart mention currently located in this trace. At 8:55:49 PM, Waverly writes, “Wyatt’s boat was hooked to his trailer? Glitch sounds like he said Tim.” Its exact reply target is unresolved. At 11:10:54 PM, Instagram user oldsaltydog1 asks under Tatum’s separate Instagram post whether Warren’s, Wyatt’s and Bart’s boats left together, and why Nolan would board a potentially sinking boat.

• July 23, 1:32:00 AM: In the Facebook replies collected from Boogie’s Tatum Part 1 copy, Lisa Jones writes, “Wyatt, Tim and this other boat need to be looked at!” The immediate reply target is unresolved. At 1:58:02 PM, Tatum publishes the original Part 3 on YouTube. Around 4:50–5:41, the guest describes Bart pulling their boat out and bringing his boat alongside. The Sea Tow call enters that towing account. At 3:55:22 PM, PLUNDER publishes Sea Tow material obtained through a records request. Its captions include, “Got to jump in and pull the plug, Bart,” putting his name in published call captions before Brantley’s later processed version.

• July 24, 5:44:05 PM: Facebook user Antionette Jackson asks under Boogie’s Tatum Part 1 copy, “Bart pulled up but I thought there were 3 other boats,did he need Bart”. At 7:37:18 PM, Tatum publishes original Part 4. At 19:52.720, its captions read, “my buddy Bart drove his boat up next to ours.” The guest describes boat assistance. At 8:19:50 PM, Facebook user Tony Williams writes under Boogie’s Part 1 copy, “BART did it “ just the name alone tells me he did it”. 

That accusation appears before Brantley’s first retained Sea Tow interpretation and before her processed-call reel. At 11:58:06 PM, Facebook user Roy Seymour pastes an MDMR report under Boogie’s separate Part 2 copy, naming Bart Edmiston Jr. and describing investigators downloading his GPS with consent.

• July 25, 3:05:18 AM: TikTok user gemma_lou writes under gods_bestgirl that “they were towed for 3 miles by their friend Bart.” That distance is the commenter’s account. At 11:10:17 AM, HYPE+ publishes another version of the released call. Its captions include, “Better jump in and pull the plug, Bart,” another published reference to his name before Brantley’s processed reel.

• July 26, 9:21:50 AM: Jeanetta Brantley publishes a Sea Tow interpretation on Facebook, describing death-related background phrases, including “OMG, is he dead?” This first retained post does not name Bart. At 5:58:11 PM, Facebook user Jason Sandison disputes that interpretation beneath her post, points readers to PLUNDER’s original, and identifies Bart as the person who helped tow the boat and was told to pull the drain plug. At 8:48:22 PM, TikTok creator gods_bestgirl connects the interview to the call: “He mentioned this person named Bart.” The video then discusses someone telling Bart to pull the plug.

• July 26, 10:02:06 PM: Ashley Brantley publishes a death-related reading of the call and says it could suggest intentional harm. Her post does not name Bart. Seventy-eight seconds later, at 10:03:24 PM, Jeanetta publishes her processed Sea Tow reel with dialogue and timecodes. Her caption describes what she personally hears “as a professional audio engineer.” It also expressly qualifies the transcription as her interpretation, rather than a definitive determination of what was said. Both the expertise claim and that qualification belong in the record.

• July 26, 10:09:51 PM: Facebook creator Kymbra Li identifies Bart Edmiston by full name and connects him to the Sea Tow audio. That is 6 minutes 27 seconds after Jeanetta’s reel; timing alone does not establish which post Li saw. At 10:12:11 PM, Facebook user Lydia Rizin writes beneath Jeanetta’s reel, “Damnit Bart, Nolan’s really dead now,” and says it made her cry. This is the earliest verified, precisely dated repeat of that reading currently held: 8 minutes 47 seconds after the reel.

• July 26, 10:21:27 PM: Facebook user Kali Yemaya writes beneath the same reel, “OMFG!!!!!! Can we cover this up?!?!!’ So Bart killed him????” At 10:34:39 PM, a Facebook user pastes the timecoded background interpretation beneath Kymbra Li’s post, including “You Killed Him” and “Damnit Bart!” The distinctive written interpretation is now appearing in another creator’s comments. At 10:38:41 PM, TikTok user vallonjimmonbell writes beneath gods_bestgirl, “I KEEP TELLING PEOPLE TO LOOK INTO BART”.

• July 27, 2:50:50 AM: TikTok user iamroyalty2u explicitly credits the enhanced call to “Janetta Breantly” and concludes, “Bart is the one who did it.” This account directly connects its accusation to Brantley’s version. At 4:22:57 AM, Threads user brit_duvenhage asks beneath dr.queenie.educates, “Who is Bart”. The host post credits Brantley for cleaning the audio. At 4:24:09 AM, brit_duvenhage writes in sjuliette707’s discussion, “Someone said dammit bart I’m wondering if that’s who hurt Nolan”.

• July 27, 5:17:01 AM: Threads user jamfour949 responds to brit_duvenhage’s question, “We need someone to figure out who Bart is…” At 5:19:35 AM, cassandrallion supplies Bart’s surname and identifies his football team in that discussion. At 6:43:52 AM, TikTok user njl.25 writes beneath gods_bestgirl, ““Dammit BART!” Was absolutely said on the enhanced clip.” At 7:04:01 AM, Threads user spacecowboy_3000 answers jamfour949 by explaining that Bart was a friend with one of the boats who helped tow the disabled boat. Identification and a corrective towing account are appearing in the same conversation.

• July 27, 8:06:25 AM: Threads user cannedass replies to cassandrallion’s identification comment, invokes “Damn it Bart,” and asks why that would be heard in a discussion of Nolan’s death. At 10:01:55 AM, Boogie THEE LowDown publishes Bart’s full name and identifies him as the person named in the call. At 12:59:50 PM, Threads user digitalkish pushes back in the identification discussion: “warren mentioned in the interview Bart brought out the 3rd boat”. At 2:59:12 PM, Threads user sjuliette707 writes, “Bart did it (whatever it is) and they all lied to cover it up. Prison for them all!”

• July 27, 3:18:12 PM: Instagram user art_dean_ supplies an enhanced-call transcription beneath The Black Wall Street Times, including “Damn Bart!” and “Nolan's really dead now”. This is that outlet’s comment section, separately from Tatum’s original and Boogie’s repost. At 5:36:02 PM, Instagram user ceeztoday writes there, “WHO IS BART?! Needs to go on a T shirt”. At 6:02:28 PM, reekie_live proposes a fight involving Bart, followed by murder and a cover-up, beginning, “This is what I think happened”.

• July 27, 8:08:58 PM: The retained Instagram record for Sarah Fields’s sarahiscensored account challenges the use of the proposed Sea Tow words as proof of killing. Its original capture receipt has not yet been matched, so that exact date is attributed to the retained account record. At 8:25:28 PM, Threads user beautifulmonster187 writes beneath briefedbyelle, “Bart going to jail”.

• July 28, 10:25:16 AM: HYPE+ publishes a video headed, “BREAKING: Nolan Wells ‘Ex-Teammate’ Bart Edmiston ACCUSED After 'Emergency Call' Leaks”. According to later reporting on the criminal complaint, July 28 is also when Brandon Ephriam Washington allegedly sends Bart and his teammates an Instagram threat about shooting people at the next game. The exact time of that alleged communication is unverified here.

• July 28, 12:59:29 PM: Instagram user rina_hinton writes beneath The Black Wall Street Times, “Bart did it”. At 3:00:20 PM, another retained sarahiscensored record names Jeanetta and criticizes her audio work and online accusations; its original capture receipt also remains unmatched. At 4:35:55 PM, Instagram user twinetime_35 asks beneath The Black Wall Street Times why Bart supposedly denied being there when the interview put him there. That alleged denial requires its own original source.

• July 28, 4:55:25 PM: Jeanetta publishes a response saying, “I don’t want anyone attacking, harassing, or engaging in personal battles with anyone on my behalf.” At 4:59:57 PM, Ashley names Sarah and says she should be the “LAST person” to speak about anyone’s past. At 5:27:56 PM, Ashley tells Sarah, “You wanted a fight, I’m bringing it to you.” At 6:08:35 PM, Ashley compares Sarah’s reaction to the audio work with a family-abuse allegation. These are personal allegations, not evidence establishing the words on the Sea Tow call. At 6:43:58 PM, Ashley describes a film intended to continue exposing Sarah.

• July 28, 8:18:31 PM: Instagram user twinetime_35 returns beneath The Black Wall Street Times and asks, “Why did Bart Lie about being there?” At 9:17:54 PM, blaznhair2021 urges people in that section to contact Bart’s university and demand his removal from football and loss of scholarships. The discussion has moved into pressure on his real-world position.

• July 28, 10:06:17 PM: Jeanetta announces that a supporter suggested creating a GoFundMe on their behalf, says it is live, and offers a contribution link. At 10:08:20 PM, TikTok user jae.louise5 posts alleged Sea Tow phrases beneath itzjustchi1, including “dam it Bart,” while saying the reading was independent of a transcription. At 10:27:02 PM, Jeanetta’s Instagram account publishes Cash App and Venmo details while saying the GoFundMe needs verification.

• July 29, 11:57:22 AM: Instagram user nunu_girl44 predicts beneath The Black Wall Street Times that “Bart gonna rat” if he cannot return to football. Attorney Russ Latino also says, in a statement dated July 29, that Bart received a credible death threat the previous day and announces legal action over accusations and identifying material. That is counsel’s account; its exact publication time is unverified here.

• July 29, 12:23:26 PM: Jeanetta says the GoFundMe was removed and Ashley created a GiveSendGo instead, connecting the support appeal to backlash, harassment and doxxing she says they experienced. At 12:23:32 PM, she repeats the account on Instagram. At 8:37:56 PM, Instagram user nicole35426 questions Sarah’s work with children beneath Ashley’s post. At 10:57:46 PM, Jeanetta’s Facebook account says the legal counsel sought could cost $150,000–$250,000 and says they were not asking for that full amount. That is a stated cost, not a record of money received.

• July 30, 2:42:05 PM: On Tatum’s live, around 10:29, a report relays counsel’s statement that “Bart helped a boat in distress and has fully cooperated with investigators”. It also reports a credible death threat. The original boat-assistance account is being repeated publicly as a correction.

• July 31, exact times unverified: Later case reporting describes Edward James Porter allegedly making 12 threatening calls to Bart and his father over roughly three hours. The allegations include threats to kill family members. Reporting also describes a text containing the family’s address and a claim that the sender was outside the home. These are alleged threats involving locating people, separately from speculation in public comments. They are allegations, not convictions.

• August 1, 11:58:25 AM: Jeanetta thanks people who sent support through Cash App. At 11:58:29 AM, she repeats the thank-you on Instagram. At 10:09:26 PM, her Facebook account supplies a Cash App handle in another comment. These records document financial-support references, without establishing amounts received.

• August 2, 10:34:00 AM: Jeanetta criticizes fundraising for legal defense in Nolan’s name and distinguishes their own fundraiser as being for legal protection and security. These are her stated distinctions.

• August 3, 2:00:49 PM: Facebook user Rissa Valdez writes beneath Christine Wonsley, “girl they already said who it was .. (Bart) listen to the audio”. The recording is offered as the answer to who was responsible. At 8:23:56 PM, Instagram user nahia_bias writes “Meth.” beneath Ashley’s Sarah-related post.

• August 4, 12:03:46 AM: Instagram user china59657 writes beneath Jeanetta’s video, “They jumped him and Bart killed him!” At 1:17:11 AM, a Nancy Grace interview re-upload is published in which Jeanetta says, around 9:44, “that name stood out to me because I hadn’t even heard that name before.” That is her account of her prior knowledge. At 1:23:47 AM, china59657 posts the same killing claim again beneath the same Jeanetta video. These are two comments by one account.

• August 4, 5:45:18 AM: TikTok user aprildenice2 writes beneath nerdypinkpanda1, “Bart did it!!!” At 9:30:12 AM, Jeanetta thanks GiveSendGo donors for helping secure legal counsel. At 9:47:55 AM, she repeats the thank-you on Instagram; at 9:48:05 AM, the Dat Gurl Netta Facebook account posts it; and at 10:21:00 AM, the TikTok copy on _datgurlnetta repeats it. These are separate crossposts carrying the same support message.

• August 4, exact time unverified: Mississippi Today reports federal charges against Edward Porter over alleged threats to a witness and another person. Later reporting identifies the Edmiston family as targets. text:
🇷🇺 🇺🇲 Putin has dug himself into a hole in Ukraine. Trump has arrived to pull him out.

The Economist delivers a severe assessment of Washington's Ukraine policy: Putin has failed to achieve a decisive battlefield victory and is now relying on a prolonged campaign of attrition, while Trump's concessions risk strengthening Moscow's position.

The criticism comes as Washington eases restrictions on Russian diesel, pressures Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries and faces renewed tensions with Zelensky over intelligence and military support.

Putin is proposing a summit with Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war, placing Ukraine's future before three major powers without Ukrainian representation.

For Moscow, the diplomatic opening comes at a critical moment. Russia has paid a high military price for limited territorial gains, while its campaign against Ukrainian energy infrastructure continues. According to a July assessment by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), Russian advances toward Kostiantynivka, Pokrovsk and Sloviansk have averaged just 50 to 90 meters per day across the offensives examined. Those rates are comparable to the grinding pace of the Battle of the Somme in 1916, one of the bloodiest campaigns of the First World War.

The human cost is impressive. CSIS estimates that Russian forces suffered approximately 1.4 million battlefield casualties between February 2022 and June 2026, including as many as 450,000 killed. Russian casualties were exceeding 30,000 per month in 2026, according to the study, while recruitment was estimated at roughly 27,000 monthly. Despite sustaining those losses, Moscow has struggled to achieve major breakthroughs, and Ukrainian counteroffensives reversed some Russian territorial gains during the spring.

Against that backdrop, reduced American pressure would offer Putin valuable strategic breathing room. Relief from energy restrictions, pressure on Kyiv to curtail strikes against Russian refineries and the prospect of negotiations with Washington and Beijing could ease some of the constraints imposed by a costly war of attrition. Moscow would gain additional diplomatic leverage at a time when its military has been unable to translate years of fighting into a decisive victory.

The Economist's warning reflects a broader concern about the direction of U.S. policy: concessions intended to bring Putin to the negotiating table may also reduce the pressure compelling him to compromise.
